item.title: Okay, I love this too; "The Walls Are Way Too Thin" (EP)
item.content:encoded:
Here are the songs from Holly Humberstone's EP The Walls Are Way Too Thin 1:

  1. Haunted House
  2. The Walls Are Way Too Thin
  3. Please Don't Leave Just Yet
  4. Thursday
  5. Scarlett
  6. Friendly Fire

Listen on Spotify

This EP gives me different impression from her album Cruel World and I love it!

I've already loved Scarlett for years, but I had never really listened to the other songs from this EP until recently.
Oh I wished I had listened to them sooner!
I love songs in this EP so much that I even looked up the guitar chords to see if I can play them.

Now I often find myself hearing especially Friendly Fire, Thursday, and Haunted House.
And I think I came to like The Walls Are Way Too Thin much more after I went to her live show this August.
Her performance was great, I'm glad that I could witness it!

item.title: Why am I more productive when I'm at a cafe?
item.content:encoded:
Writing, reading, thinking about how I want to alter this website… I can focus on those activities more in a cafe than doing them from home.

I think it's because there are less distractions when I'm at a cafe, for I don't bring my tablet with me and I use my phone less. Clutters in my room also seem to bother me.

One of other possible reasons is that there's a time limit and you can't stay there forever. When I have time at home, it feels like I can start or continue whenever I want. And because I feel that way, it's harder to start the things I want to do, I'd be like “it doesn't have to be done right now.”

Or maybe, the beverage I order at a cafe usually contains caffeine and sugar, so it boosts my focus and energy.

But I don't want to be the person who needs to go to a cafe every time when there's a work that needs to be done…
Maybe things like below might help me be more productive at home:

  • Setting up a dedicated space where there is no clutter or stuff in my sight.
  • Planning how much I work on the target task beforehand.

item.title: How I want my funeral to be like

content:encoded.p:
Sometimes, I think about how I want my funeral to be like.
I think about it when I attend or see someone's funeral, or when I read books on death.

One thing that always comes to my mind is that I don't want to keep people stuck in one place FOR ME (I don't know if there will be any guests at funeral or whether there will be a funeral in the first place).
Aren't there so many better things to do instead?
It's not like I can get up from a coffin and say goodbye...
I don't think my death will be something to be sad about, I will just be "someone who passed by".
But if there will be my funeral, I want it to be as small as possible.

item.title: I love the casts' interactions, I find my self smiling without knowing: Popular Serizawa Acts Weird Around Me

content:encoded.p: Recently I'm obsessed with the series Popular Serizawa Acts Weird Around Me .

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/II40oNJRnPA?si=M2ASw5SVBSwAsRmu" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
I watched the episode 6 everyday while it was available for free (I know I watched it too many times).

I wasn't that interested in the series at first, but I started watching clips from Instagram Live of the actors[^1] and I came to have fun while watching their interactions.
Now I can tell how close they became through shooting the series, and they always make me laugh so hard in every Instagram Live.
I found out that there are many ad-lib scenes thanks to them, and now I watch the series thinking "Is this ad-lib too?", it's fun.

Normally I can't stand watching romantic scenes, it feels cheesy and makes me want to scratch my skin. But I could watch those scenes when I play the Instagram Live at the same time (it's more like I watch the whole episode to understand what they are talking about in the stream).
I began to like the series itself too, especially because:

ul.li: Serizawa's friends' ad-lib scenes are incredibly hilarious
It's thirty-minute long. My attention span is getting short these days so I don't think I would have been able to keep focusing if it was an hour for each episodes...
The story isn't so depressing (it can be frustrating for some people for sure, but I find it hilarious) I can watch it peacefully.[^2]
The acting of Kousaku (who plays Suzuki) is impressive.
I love the interactions of Saeki and his girlfriend. I hope they are happy forever 🫶

content:encoded.p: Since I don't live in Kansai area, I can't watch it on TV and I'm a bit sad about it...
The series is not over yet, but I really hope there's season 2.

item.title: My favorite duo - "Astrid et Raphaëlle"

content:encoded.p: I always thought having a favorite series in my target language is one of the best ways to learn it (at least for me).
I've been learning French for a while, and I wanted to find something I would love, so that I can watch it on repeat and immerse myself in French.
A few months ago I found the perfect series for me, it's Astrid et Raphaëlle ! [^1]

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/kpty05_39Lo?si=lK9JhH71mwWFdURS" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
Raphaëlle, who works at a police department, and Astrid, who loves solving murder mysteries team up and solve cases together.

What I love about this series is that the friendship of these two of course! Astrid slowly starts to adapt to the new friendship and begin to be accepted by the team, and Raphaëlle's sincere attitude on learning about autism (Astrid has autism and she faces difficulties in the process of investigating) is admirable.
Raphaëlle is such a good friend, she supports Astrid and stays patient when Astrid is having a hard time, and most of all, she loves Astrid for who she is.

Astrid cares about Raphaëlle as well, and she expresses it in her own way. It's hard to tell how she feels sometimes (even she herself doesn't know), but it's certain that Raphaëlle is one of the few people who can enter Astrid's safe space (a.k.a. paper room).
Every little movement she makes feel adorable to me now, and sometimes funny. I never get tired of watching her! Even when someone else's in focus, I keep looking for Astrid to see what she's doing haha.
It's not very common to find series that two female lead the story, build genuine friendship and support each other.
It's a great series.

ul.li: Astrid et Raphaëlle - Les épisodes en replay | France TV
Astrid et Raphaëlle (TV Series 2019– ) - IMDb

content:encoded.p: [^1]: The title for English version is Astrid.

item.title: Sometimes it's painful for me to do the things I must get done

content:encoded.p:
When I was a student, I got good grades in the subject I liked but I was having a hard time keeping up with the ones I wasn't interested in.
I knew that I had to study every subject equally, but I just couldn't bring myself to do that. It felt like dragging a labrador retriever refusing to move.
I know that once I start I wouldn't feel this way, but the act of starting often feels a lot to me. It's almost suffocating.
This tendency of not being able to start things I'm not interested in had huge effects on my life (e.g. taking entrance exams and job hunting).
After I started working as a software developer I managed to do what I was assigned to with the help of the environment(I think I got often hyper fixated) but I ended up having a burnout.

I read How the Interest-Based Nervous System Shapes ADHD Motivation and Burnout by Dr. Megan Anna Neff, and now I think these struggles of mine might be a sign that I have interest based nervous system. I think her post helped me understand this trait of mine better, but will I ever learn to deal with this? Do I have to live with it for the rest of my life?

ul.li: Dr. Megan Anna Neff, How the Interest-Based Nervous System Shapes ADHD Motivation and Burnout | NDI (last accessed: 2026-10-09)

item.title: Backrooms: It's good, but I got motion sickness

content:encoded.p: This month, I finally watched the movie "Backrooms". Since I watched the YouTube series in June, I had been wanting to watch it.
I had never watched a horror movie in a movie theater before, and I'm kind of glad that this time became my first.

I was surprised to see that there were not only adults but also kids in the audience. I wouldn't have been able to watch it if I was a kid(I heard a kid crying behind my seat when Captain Clark started chasing Mary. Poor kid).
It was exciting to find some elements that had appeared in the series! I could enjoy the movie more because I had watched the series beforehand.

However, I couldn't enjoy the first part of the movie to be honest... I got pretty heavy motion sickness from the video footages. I felt conflicted because I wanted to get out and take breaks, but if I did I would have missed important scenes (as the story progressed I felt better and could focus on the screen).
Oh and I got a sticker when I passed the entrance!

item.title: Why do I write? Do I even like writing?

content:encoded.p: It's been months since I started writing here, but to be honest I don't know if I even like writing.

I know I like discovering new things and places. The excitement I get from exploring those things is stronger than any other activities.
I thought I liked singing, but I realized that I liked it only when I felt I could sing well, and not when I was practicing.
Sure it feels better after I write down my thoughts and feelings on paper, but the act of writing itself does not feel as great as exploring or singing (it doesn't feel bad either though).
And yet I write anyway, because I hear that writing helps you think, reflect on your day, organize your feelings, deal with stress and understand the world around you better.
Also, sometimes it's fun to read things you wrote in the past.

li.a: Note to self: please think on paper, for goodness' sake

item.title: I buy less books lately

content:encoded.p: This May, I wrote that I buy way more books than I can read.
I still buy books, but I buy less these days.
Maybe it's because I go to bookstores more often than I used to and I keep seeing the same books on the shelves, or maybe I'm more into the actual act of reading.

It's also possible that after I became unemployed, my savings are decreasing and I feel that I need to keep myself from spending too much money.
(Or maybe I'm just tired...)
I don't think this is a bad thing, it's not like I'm out of books to read. YET.
Despite all, bookstores are still my favorite place.

li.a: I buy way more books than I can read

item.title: DAVE THE DIVER: such a fun game!

content:encoded.p: I bought DAVE THE DIVER this summer.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/p85VHMpE0to?si=PBn7SqdxqJnTYEG3" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
I've finished playing all the chapters already so these days I mostly hunt for sharks (call me a shark hunter!).

As the story progressed, more features became available and I enjoyed them VERY MUCH.
There are so many places to explore, sub-tasks to do, fish to catch...
It's so satisfying that I feel it's worth more than 2400 yen! I don't know if I can find a game as fun as this one.

One of the things I found funny is that Dave's body shape never seemed to change.
I mean, he dives every day and works at night so he burns a lot of calories. And yet, he doesn't get muscular!
